To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“TEM is a powerful tool to study GAA NWs and to investigate the strain distribution along the NWs during the fabrication process.”
TEM analysis is a powerful tool for the investigation of nanowire devices and the study of strain at nanoscale is crucial in the development of these novel devices.

TEM analyses of GAA NWs devices are particularly challenging due the dimensions of the nanowires which are smaller than a typical TEM specimen; strain in the GAA NW devices is restored after the fin-revealing and source/drain deposition and maintained till nanowire release.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of advanced TEM techniques and their application to the investigation of nanowire devices for future CMOS technology nodes.
the investigation of strain and morphology of GAA NWs at different stages of fabrication.
the development of a new TEM-based methodology to investigate the strain distribution in GAA NW devices and to evaluate its evolution during the fabrication process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

strain engineering in the GAA NW devices is a powerful tool for improving their performances and that the combination of TEM and 3D imaging techniques is a very effective approach for the analysis of such structures.
TEM analyses are crucial in the development of GAA NWs, to investigate strain and to understand its evolution along the process steps, in order to achieve devices with the desired performances.
the strain state in GAA NWs is not uniform and depends on the fabrication steps and on the position of the TEM lamella.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TEM analyses of GAA NWs is possible and can be very useful in device characterization.
TEM analyses are essential to understand the impact of different process steps on the final GAA NWs shape and size, to evaluate strain and diffusion of materials in these structures.
the TEM analyses of these nanowires are very demanding but the results are crucial for the development of these devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TEM analysis is a powerful tool for the characterization of GAA NW devices and the understanding of the mechanisms that govern the performance of these novel devices.
TEM analysis can be used to investigate GAA NWs and that the combination of different TEM techniques is required in order to obtain a full characterization of these devices.
the strain state of GAA NWs can be controlled during the fabrication process by using different etching and deposition techniques and that TEM analyses are a powerful tool to monitor this control.
